title: The Two-Edged Sword of the Saints
english: The only-begotten Word of God is the horn of the people, to whom the holy ones, when they call out, say: 'We gore our enemies with you.' Therefore also the Word was named one-horned, according to the glory of being one-horned. Concerning this it is said: 'There I will cause a horn to rise up for David, I have prepared a lamp for my Christ' (Ps 131:17); for he showed in opposition that the Christ, who is to be born according to the flesh from the seed of David, is a horn, and he ordains it not as the sun and light to rise again. This, therefore, the horn says, will lift up his people, so that having been lifted up, it may become manifest to all the nations.

But it is for the holy alone to sing, not for the sinners, since: 'Not a beautiful song in the mouth of a sinner' (Ps 149:2); for praise is due to the upright. And who are the holy whose song it is, or the discerning sons of Israel who have God in their mind, or those who are called the people approaching God? Those having an enlightened mind and a pure soul approach God by relationship and disposition, being near the exhortation of the one who said: 'Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you' (James 4:8). And it is not by chance that this is so; for it is said concerning the hierophant Moses, what alone approaches God.

Only those having clothed themselves with the new man are able to attain the newness of mind and to do the things of the new covenant, serving by the newness of spirit and not by the oldness of the letter. These same also fulfill the assembly of the holy, accomplishing the faithful and holy things of David and having the most holy righteousness toward God; therefore also the praise does not attain the newness in the assembly of these.

The holy ones, having accomplished this, will rejoice in the glory that is to come and is eternal, even as they are called by that name from it (Ps 149:4). For we reckon, as the apostle says, that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy of the glory that is about to be revealed to us (Rom 8:18). And it is possible to hear of the glory in which the holy ones boast, concerning which it is said: 'The glory of the Lord shall be seen' (Isa 60:1), and 'The glory of your God has risen upon you' (Isa 60:1), not any other than the radiance of the glory of...

Of God. Therefore it is also written, 'Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.' Sleeping together with this glory and wisdom, the holy ones shall boast; for it is said, 'Whenever you sleep, let wisdom be with you'; appropriately to these things you say, 'Honor her, so that she may embrace you.' He who sleeps together with this is without fear and without care, and rejoices at his bed. Therefore all the souls of his holy ones, his brides, being joined together with God the Word, as a bride to the bridegroom of every rational nature, rejoice at their beds (Ps 149:6,7).

The elevations of God, demonstrated through them and through theology, in the noetic throat of the holy ones, happen to be lifting up His name to the same degree. For praising with much truth, they glorify and highly exalt Him, having in their hands two-edged swords, although they are not killing according to men, but are ready to avenge every disobedience, since the weapons of their warfare are not fleshly but are powerful through God, by which they cleanse every seductive fortification through the utterance of high words being raised against the knowledge of God.

And it is also possible to call the two-edged swords in their hands 'two-mouthed'; for the holy ones do not possess each word as two-mouthed, but according to the living and active Word of God, they are more two-mouthed than any sword. Therefore also those using the words of truth do not only cut away the false and the superfluous by loosening sophisms, but they also wound the hearers into the questions of the truth. It is possible to call both types of two-edged swords in the hands of the holy ones found in these practices. And it is possible to call even an exhortatory word a two-edged sword, doing both: rebuking the one who receives it unto repentance, and avenging and punishing the disobedient unto the end.

He does not say that the holy ones make vengeance that leads to destruction upon the Gentiles, but rather the vengeance that happens well upon them, just as the Gentiles and idolaters happen to be, so that, having cast off the life of the nations, they might become fellow-citizens of the saints and become members of God. Therefore

title: The Power of the Word and the Trumpet of Resurrection
english: And also reproaches will be active among the nations, since the vengeance upon the nations is a greater evil than the reproaches of the people, but the reproaches are against the better peoples. For [it is said]: Reprove the wise, and he will love you; make known to the righteous, and he will add to the receiving. For the peoples will not hate those reproving them because they do not happen to be evil, even if they sin through inadvertence, as opposed to those having a hateful disposition toward those reproving them because of perfected wickedness. If it is therefore said, Do not reprove the evil, lest they hate you.

You will find this same interpretation also in the Gospel, understanding the word of the Savior as saying: If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone; and if he listens to you, you have gained your brother; but if he does not listen to you, take one or two, and if he listens to them, announce it to the church; but if he even despises even the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector (Matt 18:15-17). This one, having become evil, having despised through all, is not to be reproved; for he will hate everyone who reproves, if he happens to be unholy.

For they will not put their hands in iron shackles those who seem glorious among them, being unable to act before being bound wickedly and acting toward the harm of many (Ps 149:8-9). But the righteous do not perform the vengeance and the reproaches or the making of the enclosure of bonds in an imprecise way, but with written judgment, bringing about the construction of true dogmas from the written oracles and the overthrow of pseudonymous knowledge. And I do not ignore that some of those who have explained this historically have taken the interpretation for the sake of a victory and trophies and hymns of praise to themselves against certain sensual enemies.

But also the comprehension of God through the divine Scriptures is a stronghold of the power of God, but it is not the power of God itself that exists. And you will perceive also this: whether the power of God is in men, or whether one partakes of the Holy Spirit: For you shall receive power of the Holy Spirit coming upon you, to the apostles (Acts 1:8).

Words are spoken by the Savior, and 'You indeed shall sit in the city,' as if you would not put on power from the height. Therefore, if anyone firmly preserves this power given to him, watching over it with care, becoming in its stability a part of it, he praises God, from whom this divine power is, and he says, 'I am able to do all things in Christ who strengthens me' (Phil 4:13). Since they are ruled by the Savior of power, and in the stability they praise him, understanding that the all-ruling powers—through which he royally creates, provides, benefits, and corrects—they praise him upon his powers.

He who is the unsearchable judgments of God and the unsearchable ways of him, the wise man, knowing according to the multitude of the unsearchable judgments, will praise him (Ps 150:2b); not because of the incomprehensibility of the judgments and the ways, as it says, 'O depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God, and your wisdom was wondered at by me' (Rom 11:33); I was strengthened, yet I am not able toward it. For I cannot contemplate the multitude of it; it becomes stronger than me, as if I were not able to assist it, being infinite and incomprehensible.

He who is not ashamed of Jesus and his words, clearly and loudly bringing forth the things of theology with boldness, praises him and his Father in a trumpet; for even the heralds of the truth have the command to proclaim the teaching more boldly and clearly, having as a trumpet to lift up their voice. For words are indeed spoken to them, 'Sound the trumpet in the trumpet, proclaim in Zion in my holy mountain' (Ps 150:3). But also the resurrection of the dead, which becomes fearful to all those rising, is signaled by a trumpet, for he says, 'The trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible' (1 Cor 15:52), and in another epistle, 'With the voice of an archangel and in the trumpet of God he shall descend from heaven' (1 Thess 4:16), in order to raise those who have slept in Christ. As the command of the resurrection being revealed to all, in order to raise the righteous and the unrighteous, is made known by the loud voice of the instruments.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Breath of Life and the True Voice
english: Likewise, the minds of God follow to be carried forth by the same instrument. Praise him with psaltery and lyre. What is the psaltery and the lyre, and what difference is said to be held between them in those things previously leading up? God is to be praised, singing in spirit and mind; for this is the psaltery; for the spirit and the mind are held together from above by God through the loftiness of dogmas. And he is to be praised also with lyre; through every power of the soul and sensation, with strings stretched, they are struck with order. For the soul was given as a lyre in those things previously read. If, however, through every activity of each member, it is struck as an alien lyre, no one would err in praising God through every action of the body.

Those carrying about the death of Jesus in the body, through which the flesh was killed, praise him with a timbrel (Ps 150:4). It has been interpreted before that the timbrel is that which was destined to be the one among the young women, the timbrel-players. For this is the body, which the soul will take up from the resurrection; it is a young woman playing the timbrel in announcing the minds of God in the standing of the heavenly ones with the myriads of the celebrating angels, as this is made manifest through the approaching word sounding, 'Praise him with timbrel, and also with dance'; for the soul dances with the powers and with all the higher creation after the resurrection, instead of a corrupt and weak and dishonorable and psychic body, having taken up an incorruptible, powerful, glorious, spiritual body. And the praising with strings and instrument is able to be the same as the praising with psaltery and lyre; for perhaps the lyre is strings, and the psaltery is the instrument.

I think it is made manifest through the praising him with loud cymbals (Ps 150:5) that it is necessary also to commemorate the Lord with voice according to utterance through theology. And there appears to me to understand this from the word of the apostle writing thus: 'I have become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal' (1 Cor 13:1); for if he says, 'If I speak not with mind but with tongue,' not interpreting the things said by the tongue for the understanding of the listener...

Having only a voice without possessing thought, so that the one speaking seems to be a barbarian, having sense of voice and sound only, he becomes to himself a bronze clanging or a resounding cymbal, striking and only making a noise in his hearing. Let us therefore glorify God, and imitating the perfect and righteous men in speech. For it is said concerning each of these: the discourse of a pious man is wisdom throughout; likewise, the mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom, and his tongue shall speak judgment, the law of God being in his heart; that is to say, he praises God also with mind and tongue and mouth.

But the cymbal sounds well if it has a careful and well-modulated voice clearly signifying things. But he says the same cymbal is driven forth with a loud noise according to the falling and becoming under the feet of the enemies. When God becomes all in all, the foretold word shall be fulfilled. For assisting our weakness, He imparts to us the notion of divine breath, just as it has been written concerning the first man: He breathed into his face the breath of life, and he became a living soul (Gen 2:7). For life and the fountain of life is the one who said, 'I am the life' (John 14:6), and concerning life it has been said to the Father, 'From you is the fountain of life' (Luke 10:42).

This breath of life, which makes blessed and sanctifies, coming into the man, shall prepare his soul to live, or to say thankfully, 'My soul lives in him.' This gift alone all shall enjoy who has received the word of Jesus and has believed in the one who sent him to the Father. For the Savior says, 'The one hearing my words and believing in the one who sent me has eternal life' (John 6:47). God offers this breath to those who have ascended far above the sensible things and tread upon them, called His people, just as the prophet says concerning him: 'Thus says the Lord God who made the heavens and established the earth, who gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who tread upon it' (Ps 150:6); it is evident what [is] the earth. And it is said also toward something ancient: 'And the breath of the Almighty is the one teaching me' (Job 32:8).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
